title.en: Volume 352 Biographies 111: Tang Ke, Li Bangyan, Yu Shen, Xue Ang, Wu Min, Wang Anzhong, Wang Xiang, Zhao Ye, Cao Fu, Geng Nanzhong, Wang Yu
title.raw: 卷三百五十二 列傳第一百十一 唐恪 李邦彥 余深 薛昂 吳敏 王安中 王襄 趙野 曹輔 耿南仲 王㝢 Volume 352 Biographies 111: Tang Ke, Li Bangyan, Yu Shen, Xue Ang, Wu Min, Wang Anzhong, Wang Xiang, Zhao Ye, Cao Fu, Geng Nanzhong, Wang Yu

sentences.zh: 唐恪 李邦彥附:余深 薛昂 吳敏 王安中 王襄 趙野 曹輔 耿南仲 王㝢

translations.literal: Tang Ke; Li Bangyan with appended biographies: Yu Shen, Xue Ang, Wu Min, Wang Anzhong, Wang Xiang, Zhao Ye, Cao Fu, Geng Nanzhong, Wang Yu
translations.idiomatic: Tang Ke; Li Bangyan, with appended biographies of Yu Shen, Xue Ang, Wu Min, Wang Anzhong, Wang Xiang, Zhao Ye, Cao Fu, Geng Nanzhong, and Wang Yu

sentences.zh: 唐恪，字欽叟，杭州錢塘人。

translations.literal: Tang Ke, style name Qinsou, was a native of Qiantang in Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Ke, whose style name was Qinsou, came from Qiantang in Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 四歲而孤，聞人言其父，輒悲泣。

translations.literal: Orphaned at four, whenever he heard others speak of his father he would weep in grief.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father at the age of four; whenever he heard anyone mention him, he would burst into tears.

sentences.zh: 以蔭登第，調郴尉。

translations.literal: He entered office by yin privilege and was assigned as Chen prefectural aide.
translations.idiomatic: He gained office through hereditary privilege and was posted as aide in Chen prefecture.

sentences.zh: 縣民有被害而屍不獲，吏執其鄰人，抑使自誣，令以為信。

translations.literal: A county commoner had been murdered but the corpse was not found; clerks seized a neighbor and coerced a false confession, and the magistrate accepted it as true.
translations.idiomatic: When a county resident was murdered and the body could not be found, the clerks seized a neighbor and forced a false confession, which the magistrate accepted as credible.

sentences.zh: 恪爭之，令曰：「否將為君累。」

translations.literal: Ke disputed this; the magistrate said, "If not, it will become a burden on you."
translations.idiomatic: Ke objected, but the magistrate said, "If you refuse, you will only bring trouble on yourself."

sentences.zh: 恪曰：「吾為尉而盜不能捕，更俾亡辜死平？」

translations.literal: Ke said, "I serve as aide yet cannot catch the thief—shall I instead let an innocent man die?"
translations.idiomatic: Ke replied, "I am the district aide and cannot even catch the thief—am I to let an innocent man die instead?"

sentences.zh: 躬出訪求，夕，若有告者，旦而得屍，遂獲盜。

translations.literal: He went out in person to investigate; in the evening there seemed to be an informant, and by dawn the corpse was found and the thief captured.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to investigate in person; that evening someone seemed to come forward with information, and by morning the body was found and the thief arrested.

sentences.zh: 知榆次，縣豪子雄於鄉，萃逋庇奸，不輸公賦，前後莫敢詰。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Yuci, a powerful youth in the county lorded over the countryside, gathering fugitives and sheltering wrongdoers, refusing to pay public levies; none before or after dared question him.
translations.idiomatic: When he governed Yuci, a powerful young man in the county dominated the countryside, harboring fugitives and shielding criminals while refusing to pay public taxes, and no one before or after him had dared challenge him.

sentences.zh: 恪以理善曉之，悟而自悔，折節為長者。

translations.literal: Ke used reason to persuade him well; he came to his senses and repented, restraining himself to become an elder of the community.
translations.idiomatic: Ke reasoned with him patiently until he understood his error, repented, and mended his ways to become a respected elder in the district.

sentences.zh: 最聞，擢提舉河東常平、江東轉運判官。

translations.literal: Rated highest in merit, he was promoted to intendant of Hedong Ever-Normal Granaries and transport vice-commissioner of Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: When his performance was rated highest, he was promoted to intendant of the Hedong Ever-Normal Granaries and transport vice-commissioner in Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 大觀中，牂牁內附，召為屯田員外郎，持節招納夷人。

translations.literal: In the Daguan era, when Zangge submitted to the court, he was summoned as vice director of the Directorate of Agriculture and, bearing credentials, received and win over the Yi peoples.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daguan period, when Zangge came under Song rule, he was summoned as vice director of the Directorate of Agriculture and sent with imperial credentials to receive and win over the tribal peoples.

sentences.zh: 夷始恫疑，衷甲以逆，恪盡去兵衛，從數十卒單行。

translations.literal: The Yi at first were fearful and suspicious and wore armor in resistance; Ke dismissed all armed escorts and went alone with only a few dozen soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The tribesmen were at first fearful and suspicious and came out in armor to resist; Ke dismissed his entire guard and went forward with only a few dozen men.

sentences.zh: 夷望見歡呼，投兵聽命。

translations.literal: When the Yi saw him they shouted in joy and cast down their weapons to obey.
translations.idiomatic: When they saw him they shouted in welcome, cast down their weapons, and submitted.

sentences.zh: 以奉使稱職，遷右司員外郎、起居舍人。

translations.literal: For fulfilling his mission he was transferred to vice director of the Right Office and attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Because he acquitted himself well on this mission, he was promoted to vice director of the Right Office and attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 迎遼使還，言河北邊備弛廢，宜及今無事，以時治之。

translations.literal: On returning from escorting the Liao envoy, he reported that Hebei frontier defenses were neglected and run down, and that while there was peace now they should be repaired in good time.
translations.idiomatic: After escorting the Liao envoy back, he reported that the Hebei frontier defenses had fallen into neglect and should be restored while the realm was still at peace.

sentences.zh: 徽宗壯之，曰：「非卿誰宜為者。」

translations.literal: Huizong was impressed and said, "If not you, who is fit for this?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong was impressed and said, "If not you, who is fit to undertake this?"

sentences.zh: 命為都轉運使，加集賢殿修撰。

translations.literal: He was appointed metropolitan transport commissioner and given the additional title Academician of the Hall for Collecting the Finest Writings.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed metropolitan transport commissioner and given the additional title of Academician in the Hall for Collecting the Finest Writings.

sentences.zh: 中貴人稱詔有所市，恪不答，憤而歸，中以他事，降直龍圖閣、知梓州。

translations.literal: A palace eunuch claimed an edict to make purchases; Ke did not respond; the eunuch returned in anger, and on another charge Ke was demoted to direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and made prefect of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: A palace eunuch claimed an edict authorizing purchases; Ke would not comply. The eunuch left in anger, and on another pretext Ke was demoted to direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and sent to govern Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 曆五年，徙滄州。

translations.literal: After five years he was transferred to Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After five years he was transferred to Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 河決，水犯城下，恪乘城救理。

translations.literal: The Yellow River burst its banks and the water threatened the city; Ke mounted the walls to organize relief.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River burst its banks and the flood threatened the city, Ke took to the walls to organize the relief effort.

sentences.zh: 都水孟昌齡移檄索船與兵，恪報水勢方惡，船當以備緩急；

translations.literal: The Director of Waterways Meng Changling sent a dispatch demanding boats and troops; Ke replied that the flood was still severe and boats should be kept for emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Changling, Director of Waterways, sent a dispatch demanding boats and troops; Ke replied that the waters were still dangerous and the boats must be held in reserve.

sentences.zh: 滄為極邊，兵非有旨不敢遣。

translations.literal: Cang was an extreme frontier; troops could not be sent without an edict.
translations.idiomatic: Cangzhou lay on the outer frontier, and he dared not dispatch troops without explicit imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 昌齡怒，劾之，恪不為動，益治水。

translations.literal: Changling was angry and impeached him; Ke was unmoved and worked all the harder at flood control.
translations.idiomatic: Changling was furious and impeached him, but Ke was unmoved and threw himself all the more into controlling the flood.

sentences.zh: 水去，城得全，詔書嘉獎。

translations.literal: When the water receded the city was preserved intact, and an edict praised his achievement.
translations.idiomatic: When the waters withdrew the city stood intact, and an imperial edict commended his achievement.

sentences.zh: 乃上疏請暫免保甲、保馬呈閱及復諸縣租，等第振貸，以寬被水之民。

translations.literal: He then memorialized asking temporary exemption from baojia and baoma inspections and restoration of county rents, graded relief loans, to ease the flood-stricken people.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial asking that baojia and baoma inspections be suspended for the time being, county rents restored, and graded relief loans issued to ease the burden on those affected by the flood.

sentences.zh: 未報，悉便宜罷行之，民大悅。

translations.literal: Before a reply came, he used his discretionary authority to suspend these measures entirely; the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Before any reply arrived, he used his discretionary authority to suspend all of these measures at once, to the great joy of the people.

sentences.zh: 進龍圖閣待制、知揚州，召拜戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was advanced to awaiting academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and made prefect of Yangzhou, then summoned and appointed vice minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to awaiting academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and appointed prefect of Yangzhou, then summoned to the capital as vice minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 京師暴水至，汴且溢，付恪治之。

translations.literal: Sudden flooding struck the capital and the Bian River was about to overflow; Ke was put in charge of managing it.
translations.idiomatic: When sudden flooding struck the capital and the Bian River was on the verge of overflowing, the court placed Ke in charge of the crisis.

sentences.zh: 或請決南堤以紓宮城之患，恪曰：「水漲堤壞，此亡可奈何，今決而浸之，是魚鱉吾民也。」

translations.literal: Some urged breaching the southern dike to relieve the threat to the palace city; Ke said, "When the water rises the dikes break—there is nothing to be done about that; to breach them now and inundate the land would be to make fish and turtles of our people."
translations.idiomatic: Some urged breaching the southern dike to spare the palace precincts; Ke said, "When the waters rise the dikes give way—that cannot be helped; but to breach them deliberately now would be to turn our people into fish and turtles."

sentences.zh: 亟乘小舟，相水源委，求所以利導之，乃決金堤注之河。

translations.literal: He quickly took a small boat, traced the source and course of the water, sought how to guide it advantageously, and breached the Jin dike to channel it into the river.
translations.idiomatic: He quickly took a small boat, traced the flood to its source, found how best to channel it, and breached the Jin dike to send the waters into the river.

sentences.zh: 浹旬水準，入對，帝勞之曰：「宗廟社稷獲安，卿之力也。」

translations.literal: Within ten days the water subsided to level; he entered audience and the emperor comforted him, saying, "The ancestral temples and altars of state are secure—it is your doing."
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days the waters had subsided; when he came before the throne the emperor praised him, saying, "The ancestral temples and the altars of state stand secure—this is your achievement."

sentences.zh: 恪再拜，因上疏言：「水，陰類也，至犯京闕，天其或者以陰盛之沴儆告陛下乎？

translations.literal: Ke bowed again and submitted a memorial saying, "Water is of the yin category; that it should reach and assail the capital gates—might Heaven perhaps be using the excess of yin to warn Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: Ke bowed again and submitted a memorial: "Water belongs to the yin principle; that it should assail the capital gates—might Heaven be warning Your Majesty through the excess of yin?

sentences.zh: 願垂意時事，益謹天戒。」

translations.literal: I pray that Your Majesty attend to current affairs and heed Heaven's warnings all the more."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to attend closely to affairs of state and heed Heaven's warning all the more carefully."

sentences.zh: 宣和初，遷尚書，帝許以二府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xuanhe era he was transferred to Minister, and the emperor promised him one of the two top offices.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xuanhe reign he was made Minister, and the emperor promised him a seat in one of the two highest councils.

sentences.zh: 為宰相王黼所陷，罷知滁州。

translations.literal: Framed by the chief councilor Wang Fu, he was dismissed to govern Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Framed by the chief councilor Wang Fu, he was dismissed and sent to govern Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 言者論其治第曆陽，擾民逾制，提舉鴻慶宮。

translations.literal: Critics charged that in building his estate at Liyang he had disturbed the people beyond regulation; he was made intendant of Hongqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Critics charged that in building his estate at Liyang he had harassed the people beyond what regulations allowed, and he was made intendant of Hongqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 五年，起知青州；

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was recalled to govern Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was recalled to govern Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 未行，召為吏部尚書，徙戶部。

translations.literal: Before he departed he was summoned as Minister of Personnel and transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart he was summoned as Minister of Personnel, then moved to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 復請外，以延康殿學士知潭州，請往錢塘掃墓，然後之官，遂改杭州，

translations.literal: He again requested an outside post; as academician of the Yankang Hall he was made prefect of Tanzhou, asked to go to Qiantang first to sweep his ancestors' tombs and then take up office, and was therefore changed to Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He again asked to leave the capital; as academician of the Yankang Hall he was appointed prefect of Tanzhou, requested leave to sweep his ancestors' graves at Qiantang before taking up his post, and was accordingly reassigned to Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，金兵入汴，李邦彥薦之，拜同知樞密院事，至則為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingkang era, when Jin troops entered Bian, Li Bangyan recommended him; he was appointed vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and on arrival became vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingkang crisis, when Jin forces entered Bian, Li Bangyan recommended him; he was appointed vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and, on arrival, became vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時進見者多論宣和間事，恪言于欽宗曰：「革弊當以漸，宜擇今日之所急者先之。

translations.literal: Many who came to audience then discussed affairs of the Xuanhe period; Ke said to Emperor Qinzong, "Reforming abuses should proceed gradually; one should choose what is most urgent today and address that first.
translations.idiomatic: Many who came before the throne were rehearsing abuses from the Xuanhe years; Ke said to Emperor Qinzong, "Reform should proceed step by step; choose what is most urgent today and deal with that first.

sentences.zh: 而言者不顧大體，至毛舉前事，以快一時之憤，豈不傷太上道君之心哉。

translations.literal: Yet the speakers paid no heed to the larger picture, going so far as to pick over past matters in detail to satisfy momentary anger—would this not wound the heart of the Retired Emperor, the Daoist Lord?
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who spoke ignored the larger picture, dredging up every past offense to satisfy a moment's anger—would that not wound the Retired Emperor, the Daoist Lord?

sentences.zh: 京、攸、黼、貫之徒既從竄斥，姑可已矣，他日邊事既定，然後白道君，請下一詔，與天下共棄之，誰曰不可。」

translations.literal: The cliques of Jing, You, Fu, and Guan have already been banished—let that suffice for now; when frontier affairs are settled another day, then inform the Daoist Lord and ask him to issue an edict joining the realm in casting them off—who would say that cannot be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Jing, You, Fu, Guan, and their followers have already been driven out—let that be enough for now; when the frontier is settled, then inform the Daoist Lord and ask him to issue an edict by which the whole realm joins in casting them off—who would say that cannot be done?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿論甚善，為朕作詔書，以此意佈告在位。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Your argument is excellent; draft an edict for Us and proclaim this intent to those in office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your argument is excellent; draft an edict for Us and proclaim this intent to all who hold office.

sentences.zh: 因賜東宮舊書萬卷，且用近比除子璟直秘閣，力辭之。

translations.literal: He was also granted ten thousand volumes from the Eastern Palace library, and by recent precedent his son Jing was made direct academician of the Secretariat; Ke declined firmly.
translations.idiomatic: He was also granted ten thousand volumes from the Eastern Palace library, and by recent precedent his son Jing was made direct academician of the Secretariat; Ke firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 八月，進拜少宰兼中書侍郎，帝注禮之甚渥。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was advanced to Junior Councilor and vice director of the Secretariat; the emperor bestowed favors on him with exceptional warmth.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was promoted to Junior Councilor and vice director of the Secretariat; the emperor showed him exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 然恪為相，無濟時大略。

translations.literal: Yet as councilor Ke had no grand strategy to rescue the times.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as chief minister Ke had no grand strategy to rescue the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 金騎再來，邀割三鎮，恪集廷臣議，以為當與者十九，恪從之。

translations.literal: Jin horsemen came again demanding the cession of three prefectures; Ke gathered the court to deliberate, and nineteen thought they should be ceded—Ke went along with them.
translations.idiomatic: Jin cavalry came again demanding the cession of three prefectures; Ke convened the court for deliberation, and nineteen of those present favored yielding them—Ke sided with the majority.

sentences.zh: 使者既行，於是諸道勤王兵大集，輒諭止令勿前，皆反旆而去。

translations.literal: Once the envoys had departed, troops from all circuits rallying to the throne gathered in great numbers; he repeatedly ordered them halted and told not to advance, and all turned their banners and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Once the envoys had set out, relief armies from every circuit gathered in force; he repeatedly ordered them to halt and not advance, and they all turned back.

sentences.zh: 洎金兵薄城下，始悔之，密言於帝曰：「唐自天寶而後屢失而復興者，以天子在外可以號召四方也。

translations.literal: When Jin troops pressed close beneath the walls he began to regret it and said secretly to the emperor, "Since the Tianbao era Tang repeatedly lost the realm yet rose again because the Son of Heaven was outside and could summon the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin army pressed against the walls he began to regret his course and said privately to the emperor, "After the Tianbao era the Tang lost their realm again and again yet recovered each time because the Son of Heaven was outside the capital and could summon the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 今宜舉景德故事，留太子居守而西幸洛，連據秦、雍，領天下親征，以圖興復。」

translations.literal: Now we should follow the Jingde precedent: leave the crown prince to hold the capital while the court moves west to Luoyang, hold Qin and Yong in succession, and lead the realm in person on campaign to plan restoration."
translations.idiomatic: We should now follow the Jingde precedent: leave the crown prince to defend the capital while the court moves west to Luoyang, secure Qin and Yong in succession, and lead the armies of the realm in person to plan restoration."

sentences.zh: 帝將從其議，而開封尹何㮚入見，引蘇軾所論，謂周之失計，未有如東遷之甚者。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to follow this plan when the Kaifeng prefect He Li entered audience and cited Su Shi's argument that of all Zhou's missteps none was worse than moving the capital east.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to accept this plan when Kaifeng prefect He Li came to audience and cited Su Shi's argument that of all the Zhou dynasty's missteps none equaled moving the capital eastward.

sentences.zh: 帝幡然而改，以足頓地曰：「今當以死守社稷。」

translations.literal: The emperor changed his mind abruptly and stamped his foot, saying, "Now we must defend the altars of state to the death."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor changed his mind at once and stamped his foot, saying, "Now we must defend the altars of state to the death."

sentences.zh: 擢㮚門下侍郎，恪計不用。

translations.literal: He Li was promoted to vice director of the Gate, and Ke's plan was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: He Li was promoted to vice director of the Gate, and Ke's plan went unused.

sentences.zh: 從帝巡城，為都人遮擊，策馬得脫，遂臥家求去。

translations.literal: Accompanying the emperor on an inspection of the walls, he was blocked and struck by the capital populace; he spurred his horse and escaped, then lay at home requesting dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: While accompanying the emperor on an inspection of the city walls he was intercepted and beaten by the people of the capital; he spurred his horse free, then lay at home and asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 御史胡舜陟繼劾其罪，謂「恪之智慮不能經畫邊事，但長於交結內侍，今國勢日蹙，誠不可以備位。」

translations.literal: The censor Hu Shunzhi then impeached his offenses, saying, "Ke's wisdom cannot plan frontier affairs; he excels only at cultivating palace eunuchs; with the state's position daily more desperate, he truly cannot hold this post."
translations.idiomatic: Censor Hu Shunzhi then impeached him, saying, "Ke's mind is unequal to planning the frontier crisis; he excels only at cultivating palace eunuchs; with the state's position daily more desperate, he truly cannot remain in office."

sentences.zh: 乃以觀文殿大學士、中太一宮使兼侍讀罷，㮚代為相。

translations.literal: He was therefore dismissed as academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature, commissioner of the Central Grand Unity Palace, and concurrent reader-in-waiting; He Li replaced him as councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed as academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature, commissioner of the Central Grand Unity Palace, and concurrent reader-in-waiting; He Li replaced him as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 京城不守，車駕至金帥營，恪曰：「計失矣。

translations.literal: When the capital could not be held and the imperial carriage went to the Jin commander's camp, Ke said, "The plan has failed.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell and the imperial carriage went to the Jin commander's camp, Ke said, "The plan has failed.

sentences.zh: 一入，將不得還。」

translations.literal: Once you enter, you will not be able to return."
translations.idiomatic: Once you enter, you will not be able to return."

sentences.zh: 既而還宮，恪迎拜道左，請入覲，㮚不可。

translations.literal: Afterward the emperor returned to the palace; Ke bowed in welcome on the roadside and asked to be received in audience; He Li would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor eventually returned to the palace; Ke bowed in welcome along the road and asked to be received in audience, but He Li would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，復幸，恪曰：「一之謂甚，其可再乎？」

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year the emperor went again; Ke said, "Once is already too much—how can it be done a second time?"
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year the emperor went again; Ke said, "Once is already too much—how can it be done a second time?"

sentences.zh: 及金人逼百官立張邦昌，令吳開、莫儔入城取推戴狀，恪既書名，仰藥而死。

translations.literal: When the Jin forced the officials to install Zhang Bangchang and sent Wu Kai and Mo Chou into the city to collect statements of support, Ke had already signed his name and took poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin forced the officials to install Zhang Bangchang and sent Wu Kai and Mo Chou into the city to collect pledges of support, Ke had already signed his name, then took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 李邦彥

translations.literal: Li Bangyan
translations.idiomatic: Li Bangyan

sentences.zh: 李邦彥，字士美，懷州人。

translations.literal: Li Bangyan, style name Shimei, was a native of Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bangyan, whose style name was Shimei, came from Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 父浦，銀工也。

translations.literal: His father Pu was a silversmith.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pu was a silversmith.

sentences.zh: 邦彥喜從進士游，河東舉人入京者，必道懷訪邦彥。

translations.literal: Bangyan delighted in associating with jinshi degree holders; candidates from Hedong entering the capital always went by way of Huai to visit Bangyan.
translations.idiomatic: Bangyan delighted in the company of jinshi scholars; examination candidates from Hedong bound for the capital always routed through Huai to call on him.

sentences.zh: 有所營置，浦亦罷工與為之，且復資給其行，由是邦彥聲譽弈弈。

translations.literal: When they had business to arrange, Pu would also stop work to help them and moreover supply their travel expenses; thus Bangyan's reputation flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they needed something arranged, Pu would lay aside his trade to assist and even fund their journey; by this means Bangyan's reputation spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 入補太學生，大觀二年，上舍及第，授秘書省校書郎，試符寶郎。

translations.literal: He entered the Imperial University as a student; in the second year of Daguan he passed the upper dormitory examination, was appointed proofreader of the Secretariat, and tested as tally officer of talismans and seals.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Imperial University; in the second year of Daguan he passed the upper dormitory examination, was appointed proofreader in the Secretariat, and tested for the post of tally officer of talismans and seals.

sentences.zh: 邦彥俊爽，美風姿，為文敏而工。

translations.literal: Bangyan was handsome and spirited, with a fine bearing, and his writing was quick and skilled.
translations.idiomatic: Bangyan was handsome and spirited, carried himself well, and wrote with quickness and skill.

sentences.zh: 然生長閭閻，習猥鄙事，應對便捷；

translations.literal: Yet having grown up in the lanes he was versed in vulgar and base matters and was quick in repartee.
translations.idiomatic: Yet having grown up in the back alleys he was versed in coarse and vulgar pursuits and answered with ready wit.

sentences.zh: 善謳謔，能蹴鞠，每輟街市俚語為詞曲，人爭傳之，自號李浪子。

translations.literal: He was skilled at ballads and jest, could play cuju, and often turned street slang into song lyrics that people vied to copy; he styled himself Li the Prodigal.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at ribald songs and jest, could play cuju, and often turned street slang into lyrics that everyone rushed to copy; he called himself Li the Prodigal.

sentences.zh: 言者劾其遊縱無檢，罷符寶郎，復為校書郎。

translations.literal: Critics impeached his unrestrained and undisciplined conduct; he was dismissed from tally officer and restored as proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: Critics impeached his unrestrained conduct; he was dismissed from the tally office and restored to proofreader.

sentences.zh: 俄以吏部員外郎領議禮局，出知河陽，召為起居郎。

translations.literal: Soon as vice director of the Ministry of Personnel he headed the Rites Bureau, was sent out to govern Heyang, and recalled as attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, as vice director of the Ministry of Personnel, he headed the Rites Bureau, was sent out to govern Heyang, and was recalled as attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 邦彥善事中人，爭薦譽之，累遷中書舍人、翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: Bangyan was adept at serving palace insiders; they vied to praise him, and he rose in succession to drafting attendant of the Secretariat and Hanlin academician and chief drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Bangyan was adept at courting palace eunuchs, who vied to praise him, and he rose in succession to drafting attendant of the Secretariat and Hanlin academician and chief drafter.

sentences.zh: 宣和三年，拜尚書右丞；

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuanhe he was appointed vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xuanhe he was appointed vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 五年，轉左丞。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to left vice director.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to left vice director.

sentences.zh: 浦死，贈龍圖閣直學士，諡曰宣簡。

translations.literal: When Pu died he was posthumously made direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall with the posthumous title Xuanjian.
translations.idiomatic: When Pu died he was posthumously made direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall with the posthumous title Xuanjian.

sentences.zh: 邦彥起復，與王黼不協，乃陰結蔡攸、梁師成等，讒黼罷之。

translations.literal: Bangyan returned from mourning; at odds with Wang Fu, he secretly joined Cai You, Liang Shicheng, and others to slander Fu until he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Bangyan returned from mourning; at odds with Wang Fu, he secretly allied with Cai You, Liang Shicheng, and others to slander Fu until he was removed.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜少宰，無所建明，惟阿順趨諂充位而已，都人目為「浪子宰相」。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Junior Councilor; he offered no constructive proposals but only flattered and fawned to fill the post; the capital people called him "the Prodigal Councilor."
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Junior Councilor; he offered no constructive policy but only flattered and fawned to hold the seat, and the people of the capital called him "the Prodigal Councilor."

sentences.zh: 徽宗內禪，命為龍德宮使，升太宰。

translations.literal: When Huizong abdicated internally he was made commissioner of the Longde Palace and promoted to Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong abdicated in favor of his son, Bangyan was made commissioner of the Longde Palace and promoted to Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 知眾議不與，外患日逼，抗疏丐宮祠。

translations.literal: Knowing that public opinion was against him and external danger daily pressed closer, he submitted a memorial begging for a palace sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that public opinion was against him and external danger drew nearer each day, he submitted a memorial begging for a palace sinecure.

sentences.zh: 金人既薄都城，李綱、种師道罷，邦彥堅主割地之議。

translations.literal: Once the Jin had pressed close to the capital and Li Gang and Zhong Shidao were dismissed, Bangyan firmly upheld the policy of ceding territory.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Jin had pressed against the capital and Li Gang and Zhong Shidao were dismissed, Bangyan firmly upheld the policy of ceding territory.

sentences.zh: 太學生陳東數百人伏宣德門上書，言邦彥及白時中、張邦昌、趙野、王孝迪、蔡懋、李乂之徒為社稷之賊，請斥之。

translations.literal: Several hundred Imperial University students led by Chen Dong lay prostrate at the Xuande Gate and submitted a memorial saying Bangyan and Bai Shizhong, Zhang Bangchang, Zhao Ye, Wang Xiaodi, Cai Mao, Li Yi, and their like were enemies of the altars of state and should be driven out.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred Imperial University students led by Chen Dong lay prostrate at the Xuande Gate and submitted a memorial naming Bangyan, Bai Shizhong, Zhang Bangchang, Zhao Ye, Wang Xiaodi, Cai Mao, Li Yi, and their like as enemies of the altars of state and demanding their removal.

sentences.zh: 邦彥退朝，群指而大詬，且欲毆之，邦彥疾驅得免。

translations.literal: As Bangyan left court the crowd pointed and cursed him loudly and were about to beat him; Bangyan spurred his horse and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: As Bangyan left court the crowd pointed at him and shouted abuse, and some tried to seize and beat him; he spurred his horse and escaped.

sentences.zh: 乃以特進、觀文殿大學士充太一宮使。

translations.literal: He was therefore made specially advanced academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and commissioner of the Grand Unity Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore made specially advanced academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and commissioner of the Grand Unity Palace.

sentences.zh: 不旬日，吳敏為請，復起為太宰。

translations.literal: Within ten days Wu Min pleaded on his behalf and he was recalled as Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days Wu Min pleaded on his behalf and he was recalled as Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 人皆駭愕，言者交論之。

translations.literal: Everyone was shocked and alarmed; critics debated him in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone was shocked and alarmed, and critics assailed him in turn.

sentences.zh: 出知鄧州，遂請持餘服，提舉亳州明道宮。

translations.literal: He was sent out to govern Dengzhou, then asked to observe the remainder of his mourning and was made intendant of Mingdao Palace in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to govern Dengzhou, then asked to complete his mourning observances and was made intendant of Mingdao Palace in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，以主和誤國，責建武軍節度副使，潯州安置。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyan era, for pursuing peace and harming the state, he was demoted to vice military commissioner of Jianwu Army and settled at Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianyan era, for having pursued peace at the cost of the state, he was demoted to vice military commissioner of the Jianwu Army and exiled to Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 方蔡京、王黼用事，附麗者多援引入政府，若余深、薛昂、吳敏、王安中、趙野，史皆逸其事，因附著於此雲。

translations.literal: When Cai Jing and Wang Fu held power, many who attached themselves to them were pulled into government; as for Yu Shen, Xue Ang, Wu Min, Wang Anzhong, and Zhao Ye, the histories have omitted their affairs, and they are therefore appended here.
translations.idiomatic: While Cai Jing and Wang Fu held power, many who attached themselves to them were drawn into high office; as for Yu Shen, Xue Ang, Wu Min, Wang Anzhong, and Zhao Ye, the histories have omitted their stories, and they are therefore recorded here.

sentences.zh: 余深 附

translations.literal: Yu Shen, appended
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shen, appended

sentences.zh: 余深，福州人。

translations.literal: Yu Shen was a native of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shen came from Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 元豐五年，進士及第。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 崇甯元年，為太常博士、著作佐郎，改司封員外郎，拜監察御史、殿中侍御史，試辟雍司業。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongning he was made erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and assistant editor, then vice director of the Bureau of Honors, and appointed investigating censor and palace censor, with trial appointment as director of studies at the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongning he was made erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and assistant editor, then vice director of the Bureau of Honors, and appointed investigating censor and palace censor, with trial appointment as director of studies at the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 累官御史中丞兼侍讀。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to censor-in-chief and concurrent reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to censor-in-chief and concurrent reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 治張懷素獄，事連蔡京，與開封尹林攄曲為掩覆，獄辭有及京者輒焚之。

translations.literal: In prosecuting the Zhang Huaisu case, which implicated Cai Jing, he and the Kaifeng prefect Lin Zhe bent the law to cover it up, burning any testimony that mentioned Jing.
translations.idiomatic: While prosecuting the Zhang Huaisu case, which implicated Cai Jing, he and Kaifeng prefect Lin Zhe bent the law to cover it up, burning any testimony that mentioned Jing.

sentences.zh: 京遂力引深與攄驟至執政。

translations.literal: Jing then strongly promoted Shen and Zhe until they swiftly reached the council.
translations.idiomatic: Jing then used all his influence to promote Shen and Zhe until they swiftly reached the highest council.

sentences.zh: 大觀二年，以吏部尚書拜尚書左丞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daguan, as Minister of Personnel he was appointed left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daguan, as Minister of Personnel he was appointed left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 三年，轉中書侍郎；

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 四年，轉門下侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to vice director of the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to vice director of the Gate.

sentences.zh: 京既致仕，深不自安，累疏請罷，乃以資政殿學士知青州。

translations.literal: Once Jing had retired, Shen felt increasingly uneasy and submitted repeated memorials asking to resign; he was therefore made academician of the Zizheng Hall and prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing retired, Shen grew increasingly uneasy and submitted memorial after memorial asking to resign; he was finally made academician of the Zizheng Hall and sent to govern Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 深諂附蔡京，結為死黨。

translations.literal: Shen fawned on and attached himself to Cai Jing, forming a sworn faction.
translations.idiomatic: Shen fawned on Cai Jing and joined him in a sworn faction.

sentences.zh: 京奸謀詭計得助多者，深為首，攄次之。

translations.literal: Of those who aided Jing's treacherous schemes and crafty plots, Shen was foremost and Zhe second.
translations.idiomatic: Among those who aided Jing's treacherous schemes and crafty plots, Shen stood foremost and Zhe second.

sentences.zh: 言者累章劾深，深益懼，丐致仕。

translations.literal: Critics submitted repeated memorials impeaching Shen; Shen grew all the more fearful and begged to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Critics submitted memorial after memorial impeaching Shen; he grew ever more fearful and begged to retire.

sentences.zh: 建炎二年，降中大夫，臨江軍居住。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyan he was demoted to grandee of court and ordered to reside at Linjiang Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianyan he was demoted to grandee of court and ordered to reside at Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 尋以渡江赦恩，還鄉里，卒。

translations.literal: Soon, through the amnesty granted for crossing the Yangzi, he returned to his home district and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, through the amnesty granted for the court's flight south across the Yangzi, he was allowed to return home and died there.

sentences.zh: 子日章，亦以言者罷徽猷閣待制。

translations.literal: His son Rizhang was also dismissed from awaiting academician of the Huixian Hall by critics.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rizhang was likewise dismissed from awaiting academician of the Huixian Hall after critics spoke against him.

sentences.zh: 薛昂 附

translations.literal: Xue Ang, appended
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ang, appended

sentences.zh: 薛昂，杭州人，登元豐八年進士第。

translations.literal: Xue Ang was a native of Hangzhou and passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Yuanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ang came from Hangzhou and passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Yuanfeng.

sentences.zh: 崇甯初，曆太學博士、校書郎、著作佐郎，為殿中侍御史，試起居郎，改中書舍人兼侍講，升給事中兼大司成。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongning he served in succession as erudite of the Imperial University, proofreader, and assistant editor, became palace censor, tested as attendant of the Secretariat, was changed to drafting attendant of the Secretariat and concurrent lecturer, and was promoted to supervising censor and concurrent grand director of studies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongning reign he rose through the posts of Imperial University erudite, proofreader, and assistant editor, became palace censor, tested as attendant of the Secretariat, was made drafting attendant and concurrent lecturer, and was promoted to supervising censor and concurrent grand director of studies.

sentences.zh: 昂寡學術，士子有用《史記》、《西漢》語，輒黜之。

translations.literal: Ang was shallow in learning; whenever a scholar used language from the Records of the Grand Historian or the History of the Former Han, he would dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: Ang was poorly learned; whenever a candidate used phrases from the Records of the Grand Historian or the History of the Former Han, he would fail him.

sentences.zh: 在哲宗時，常請罷史學，哲宗斥為俗佞。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Zhezong he often asked to abolish the study of history; Zhezong denounced him as a vulgar flatterer.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhezong he repeatedly petitioned to abolish the study of history; Zhezong denounced him as a vulgar sycophant.

sentences.zh: 拜翰林學士，以不稱職改刑部尚書，轉兵部。

translations.literal: He was appointed Hanlin academician; for incompetence he was changed to Minister of Justice, then transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Hanlin academician; found unfit for the post, he was moved to Minister of Justice and then to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 大觀三年，拜尚書左丞。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daguan he was appointed left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daguan he was appointed left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年，請補外，出知江甯，徙河南。

translations.literal: The next year he asked for an outside post, was sent out to govern Jiangning, and was transferred to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he asked for a provincial post, was sent to govern Jiangning, and was then transferred to Henan.

sentences.zh: 久之，提舉嵩山崇福宮。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was made intendant of Chongfu Palace on Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was made intendant of Chongfu Palace on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 政和三年，蔡京復用事，昂復自尚書右丞為左丞，遷門下侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenghe, when Cai Jing again held power, Ang was restored from right vice director to left vice director and promoted to vice director of the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenghe, when Cai Jing returned to power, Ang was restored from right vice director to left vice director and promoted to vice director of the Gate.

sentences.zh: 尋請罷，授彰化軍節度使、佑神觀使，改特進，充資政殿大學士、知應天府。

translations.literal: Soon he asked to resign and was made military commissioner of Zhanghua Army and commissioner of the Youshen Palace, then specially advanced and made academician of the Zizheng Hall and prefect of Yingtianfu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he asked to resign and was made military commissioner of Zhanghua and commissioner of the Youshen Palace, then given special advancement and made academician of the Zizheng Hall and prefect of Yingtianfu.

sentences.zh: 昂與余深、林攄始終附會蔡京，至舉家為京諱。

translations.literal: Ang, with Yu Shen and Lin Zhe, attached themselves to Cai Jing from beginning to end, going so far as to have their whole households avoid Jing's taboo name.
translations.idiomatic: Ang, together with Yu Shen and Lin Zhe, clung to Cai Jing from first to last, going so far as to have their entire households avoid speaking Jing's taboo name.

sentences.zh: 或誤及之。

translations.literal: If someone erred and mentioned it,
translations.idiomatic: If anyone accidentally mentioned it,

sentences.zh: 輒加笞責，昂嘗誤及，即自批其口。

translations.literal: he would add beating with the rod; Ang once erred himself and immediately struck his own mouth.
translations.idiomatic: he would have them beaten; Ang once made the mistake himself and at once slapped his own mouth.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，言者斥其罪，詔以金紫光祿大夫致仕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingkang critics denounced his crimes and an edict ordered him to retire as grandee of the golden-girdled purple.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingkang crisis critics denounced his crimes, and an edict ordered him to retire with the rank of grandee of the golden-girdled purple.

sentences.zh: 杭州軍亂，昂不請命領州事，責徽州居住。

translations.literal: When Hangzhou troops mutinied, Ang did not request orders to take charge of the prefecture and was ordered to reside at Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hangzhou garrison mutinied, Ang failed to request authority to take charge of the prefecture and was ordered to reside at Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 昂主王氏學，嘗在安石坐，圍棋賭詩，局敗，昂不能作，安石代之，時人以為笑雲。

translations.literal: Ang championed the Wang clan learning; he once sat with Wang Anshi playing go and wagering poems; when he lost the game Ang could not compose, and Anshi wrote in his place—people at the time took it as a laughing matter.
translations.idiomatic: Ang championed the Wang school of learning; he once sat with Wang Anshi playing go for wagers in verse; when he lost the game he could not compose a poem, and Anshi wrote one for him—people at the time made it a laughingstock.

sentences.zh: 吳敏 附

translations.literal: Wu Min, appended
translations.idiomatic: Wu Min, appended

sentences.zh: 吳敏，字元中，真州人。

translations.literal: Wu Min, style name Yuanzhong, was a native of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Min, whose style name was Yuanzhong, came from Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 大觀二年，辟雍私試首選。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daguan he ranked first in the Directorate of Education's private examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daguan he ranked first in the Directorate of Education's private examination.

sentences.zh: 蔡京喜其文，欲妻以女，敏辭。

translations.literal: Cai Jing admired his writing and wished to give him his daughter in marriage; Min declined.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing admired his writing and wished to marry his daughter to him; Min declined.

sentences.zh: 因擢浙東學事司幹官，為秘書省校書郎，京薦之充館職。

translations.literal: He was therefore promoted to secretary of the Zhedong Directorate of Education and made proofreader of the Secretariat; Jing recommended him to fill a post in the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore promoted to secretary of the Zhedong Directorate of Education and made proofreader in the Secretariat; Jing recommended him for a Hanlin post.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎劉正夫以敏未嘗過省，不可，京乃請御筆特召上殿，除右司郎官。

translations.literal: The vice director of the Secretariat Liu Zhengfu objected that Min had never passed the provincial examination and could not be appointed; Jing then asked for an imperial brush summons to audience and had him appointed vice director of the Right Office.
translations.idiomatic: Vice director of the Secretariat Liu Zhengfu objected that Min had never passed the provincial examination and could not be appointed; Jing then requested an imperial-brush summons to audience and secured his appointment as vice director of the Right Office.

sentences.zh: 御筆自此始，違者以大不恭論，繇是權幸爭請御筆，而繳駁之任廢矣。

translations.literal: The imperial brush began from this time; violators were charged with great disrespect; hence the powerful and favored vied to request imperial-brush appointments, and the duty of review and rejection was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial-brush appointment began at this point; anyone who violated the procedure was charged with great disrespect; from then on the powerful and favored vied to request imperial-brush appointments, and the duty of review and rejection fell into disuse.

sentences.zh: 升中書舍人、同修國史，改給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to drafting attendant of the Secretariat and concurrent editor of the national history, then changed to supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to drafting attendant of the Secretariat and concurrent editor of the national history, then made supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 敏為蔡京所引，鄭居中方秉政，敏數言其失，居中銜之。

translations.literal: Min was introduced by Cai Jing; when Zheng Juzhong held power, Min often spoke of his faults and Juzhong resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Min had been introduced by Cai Jing; when Zheng Juzhong held power, Min often criticized his failings and Juzhong bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 坐駁盜當死者，罷為右文殿修撰、提舉南京鴻慶宮。

translations.literal: For rejecting a death sentence in a robbery case he was dismissed as academician of the Youwen Hall and made intendant of Hongqing Palace in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: For overturning a death sentence in a robbery case he was dismissed as academician of the Youwen Hall and made intendant of Hongqing Palace in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 久之，復為給事中、權直學士院兼侍講。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was again made supervising censor, acting head of the Academy of Letters, and concurrent lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was again made supervising censor, acting head of the Academy of Letters, and concurrent lecturer.

sentences.zh: 徽宗將內禪，蔡攸探知上意，引敏入對。

translations.literal: When Huizong was about to abdicate internally, Cai You probed the emperor's intent and brought Min in for audience.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong was about to abdicate, Cai You discerned the emperor's intent and brought Min in for audience.

sentences.zh: 宰臣執政皆在，敏前奏事，且曰：「金人渝盟，舉兵犯順，陛下何以待？」

translations.literal: The chief councilors and those in power were all present; Min spoke first and said, "The Jin have violated the treaty and raised troops in rebellion—how does Your Majesty intend to respond?"
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers and those in power were all present; Min spoke first and said, "The Jin have broken the treaty and marched in rebellion—how does Your Majesty mean to respond?"

sentences.zh: 上蹙然曰：「奈何！」

translations.literal: The emperor frowned and said, "What is to be done!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor frowned and said, "What can be done!"

sentences.zh: 時東幸計已定，命戶部尚書李棁先出守金陵。

translations.literal: At that time the plan to move east was already settled; the emperor ordered Minister of Revenue Li Zhi to go out first to hold Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: By then the plan to move the court east was already settled; the emperor ordered Minister of Revenue Li Zhi to go out first to defend Jinling.

sentences.zh: 敏退，詣都堂言曰：「朝廷便為棄京師計，何理也？

translations.literal: Min withdrew and went to the chief councilors' hall, saying, "The court is already planning to abandon the capital—what sense is there in that?
translations.idiomatic: Min withdrew and went to the chief ministers' hall, saying, "The court is already preparing to abandon the capital—how can that be justified?

sentences.zh: 此命果行，須死不奉詔。」

translations.literal: If this order is truly carried out, I must die rather than obey it."
translations.idiomatic: If this order is truly issued, I would rather die than obey it."

sentences.zh: 宰執以為言，棁遂罷行。

translations.literal: The chief councilors spoke on his behalf and Li Zhi's departure was halted.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers took up his argument and Li Zhi's mission was canceled.

sentences.zh: 皇太子除開封尹，上去意益決，敏因奏對得請，遂薦李綱。

translations.literal: The crown prince was made acting prefect of Kaifeng; as the emperor's resolve to leave grew firmer, Min secured permission through audience and then recommended Li Gang.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was made acting prefect of Kaifeng; as the retired emperor's resolve to flee grew firmer, Min secured permission through audience and recommended Li Gang.

sentences.zh: 綱嘗語敏以上宜傳位，如唐天寶故事，故薦之，冀上或有所問也。

translations.literal: Gang had once told Min that the emperor ought to pass the throne as in the Tianbao precedent of Tang, so he recommended him hoping the emperor might question him.
translations.idiomatic: Gang had once told Min that the emperor ought to pass the throne as in the Tang Tianbao precedent, so Min recommended him in the hope that the emperor might consult him.

sentences.zh: 明日，宰臣奏事，徽宗獨留李邦彥，語敏所對。

translations.literal: The next day when the chief councilors reported to audience, Huizong kept only Li Bangyan and spoke of Min's responses.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, when the chief ministers reported to audience, Huizong kept only Li Bangyan and discussed Min's answers.

sentences.zh: 命除門下侍郎，輔太子。

translations.literal: He ordered Min appointed vice director of the Gate to assist the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Min appointed vice director of the Gate to assist the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 敏駭曰：「臣既畫計，當從陛下巡幸。

translations.literal: Min was alarmed and said, "Your servant has already drawn up the plan and ought to accompany Your Majesty on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Min was alarmed and said, "I have already devised the plan and ought to accompany Your Majesty on the journey.

sentences.zh: 陛下且傳位，而臣受不次之擢，臣曷敢？」

translations.literal: Your Majesty is about to pass the throne, yet your servant receives an extraordinary promotion—how dare I accept it?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is about to pass the throne, yet I am given an extraordinary promotion—how dare I accept it?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「不意卿乃爾敢言。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I did not expect you to speak so boldly."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I did not expect you to be so bold in speech."

sentences.zh: 於是命敏草傳位詔。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered Min to draft the abdication edict.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore ordered Min to draft the abdication edict.

sentences.zh: 王安中 附

translations.literal: Wang Anzhong, appended
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anzhong, appended

sentences.zh: 王安中，字履道，中山陽曲人。

translations.literal: Wang Anzhong, style name Lüdao, was a native of Yangqu in Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anzhong, whose style name was Lüdao, came from Yangqu in Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 進士及第，調瀛州司理參軍、大名縣主簿，曆秘書省著作郎。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as judicial aide in Yingzhou and registrar of Daming County, serving in succession as editor in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as judicial aide in Yingzhou and registrar of Daming County, then served in succession as editor in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 政和間，天下爭言瑞應，廷臣輒箋表賀，徽宗觀所作，稱為奇才。

translations.literal: In the Zhenghe era, when the realm vied to report auspicious omens and court ministers repeatedly submitted congratulatory memorials, Huizong read what Anzhong had written and praised him as a rare talent.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenghe era, when the whole realm vied to report auspicious omens and court ministers repeatedly submitted congratulatory memorials, Huizong read Anzhong's compositions and called him a rare talent.

sentences.zh: 他日，特出制詔三題使具草，立就，上即草後批：「可中書舍人。」

translations.literal: Another day he specially set three topics for drafting edicts and had him complete them on the spot; the emperor immediately annotated on the draft: "May be made drafting attendant of the Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion he specially set three topics for drafting edicts and required immediate completion; the emperor annotated the draft at once: "May be made drafting attendant of the Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 未幾，自秘書少監除中書舍人，擢御史中丞。

translations.literal: Before long, from vice director of the Secretariat he was made drafting attendant and promoted to censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he rose from vice director of the Secretariat to drafting attendant and was promoted to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 開封邏卒夜跡盜，盜脫去，民有驚出與卒遇，縛以為盜；

translations.literal: Kaifeng patrol guards tracked thieves by night; the thieves escaped, and a startled civilian who ran out met the guards and was bound as a thief.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng patrol guards tracked thieves by night; the thieves escaped, and a startled civilian who ran out into the street met the guards and was bound as a thief.

sentences.zh: 民訟諸府，不勝考掠之慘，遂誣服。

translations.literal: The man sued at the prefectural office but could not endure the cruelty of torture and falsely confessed.
translations.idiomatic: The man brought suit at the prefectural office but could not endure the cruelty of the beating and falsely confessed.

sentences.zh: 安中廉知之，按得冤狀，即出民，抵吏罪。

translations.literal: Anzhong learned of the injustice through investigation, established the wrongful case, released the man, and punished the clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhong investigated and found the injustice, established that the case was wrongful, released the man, and punished the officers responsible.

sentences.zh: 有徐禋者，以增廣鼓鑄之說媚于蔡京，京奏遣禋措置東南九路銅事，且令搜訪寶貨。

translations.literal: There was one Xu Yin who, through proposals to expand drum-casting, flattered Cai Jing; Jing memorialized sending Yin to arrange copper affairs in the nine southeastern circuits and also ordered him to search out precious goods.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Xu Yin won Cai Jing's favor with proposals to expand drum-casting; Jing memorialized sending Yin to manage copper affairs in the nine southeastern circuits and ordered him to search out precious goods as well.

sentences.zh: 禋圖繪坑冶，增舊幾十倍，且請開洪州嚴陽山坑，迫有司承歲額數十兩。

translations.literal: Yin mapped out mining sites and increased the old quotas nearly tenfold, and asked to open the Yanyang Mountain mine in Hongzhou, forcing the relevant offices to meet an annual quota of several tens of taels.
translations.idiomatic: Yin mapped out mining sites and increased the old quotas nearly tenfold, and petitioned to open the Yanyang Mountain mine in Hongzhou, forcing the relevant offices to meet an annual quota of several tens of taels.

sentences.zh: 其所烹煉，實得銖兩而已。

translations.literal: What he actually smelted and refined amounted to only a few ounces.
translations.idiomatic: What he actually smelted and refined amounted to only a few ounces.

sentences.zh: 禋術窮，乃妄請得希世珍異與古之寶器，乞歸書藝局，京主其言。

translations.literal: When Yin's methods were exhausted he falsely claimed to have obtained rare treasures of the age and ancient precious vessels and begged to return them to the Bureau of Calligraphy and Painting; Jing backed his claim.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin's methods failed he falsely claimed to have obtained rare treasures of the age and ancient precious vessels and begged to turn them over to the Bureau of Calligraphy and Painting; Jing backed his claim.

sentences.zh: 安中獨論禋欺上擾下，宜令九路監司覆之，禋竟得罪。

translations.literal: Anzhong alone argued that Yin was deceiving the emperor above and harassing the people below, and that the supervisory commissioners of the nine circuits should be ordered to review the matter; Yin was finally found guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhong alone argued that Yin was deceiving the emperor above and harassing the people below, and urged that the supervisory commissioners of the nine circuits be ordered to investigate; Yin was finally found guilty.

sentences.zh: 時上方鄉神仙之事，蔡京引方士王仔昔以妖術見，朝臣戚裏寅緣關通。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was inclined toward immortals; Cai Jing introduced the Daoist Wang Zaixi, who appeared with sorcery; court ministers and imperial kin curried favor through him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor was devoted to immortals; Cai Jing introduced the Daoist Wang Zaixi, who appeared with sorcery, and court ministers and imperial kin curried favor through him.

sentences.zh: 安中疏請自今招延山林道術之士，當責所屬保任，宣召出入，必令察視其所經由，仍申嚴臣庶往還之禁；

translations.literal: Anzhong submitted a memorial asking that from now on whenever mountain recluses and Daoist masters were recruited, the responsible office should be required to vouch for them; when summoned in and out they must be made to declare their route, and strict prohibitions on contact between officials and commoners should be announced.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhong submitted a memorial asking that from then on, whenever mountain recluses and Daoist masters were recruited, the responsible office should be required to vouch for them; those summoned to court must declare their routes in and out, and strict limits on contact between officials and the public should be enforced.

sentences.zh: 並言京欺君僭上、蠹國害民數事。

translations.literal: He also listed several charges of Jing's deceiving the ruler, overstepping authority, and harming the state and the people.
translations.idiomatic: He also listed several charges of Jing's deceiving the ruler, overstepping his authority, and harming the state and the people.

sentences.zh: 上悚然納之。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted this with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this with alarm.

sentences.zh: 已而再疏京罪，上曰：「本欲即行卿章，以近天寧節，俟過此，當為卿罷京。」

translations.literal: Soon he submitted another memorial on Jing's crimes; the emperor said, "I originally intended to act on your memorial at once, but as the Tianning festival is near, after it passes I will dismiss Jing for you."
translations.idiomatic: Soon he submitted another memorial on Jing's crimes; the emperor said, "I originally meant to act on your memorial at once, but with the Tianning festival near, after it passes I will dismiss Jing for you."

sentences.zh: 京伺知之，大懼，其子攸日夕侍禁中，泣拜懇祈。

translations.literal: Jing learned of this and was greatly afraid; his son You waited on the emperor in the inner palace day and night, weeping and begging.
translations.idiomatic: Jing learned of this and was terrified; his son You attended the emperor in the inner palace day and night, weeping and pleading for mercy.

sentences.zh: 上為遷安中翰林學士，又遷承旨。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore transferred Anzhong to Hanlin academician, then to chief drafter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore transferred Anzhong to Hanlin academician, then to chief drafter.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，言者論其締合王黼、童貫及不幾察郭藥師叛命，罷為觀文殿大學士、提舉嵩山崇福宮；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingkang critics charged that he had bonded with Wang Fu and Tong Guan and had failed to detect Guo Yaoshi's rebellion in time; he was dismissed as academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and made intendant of Chongfu Palace on Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jingkang critics charged that he had bonded with Wang Fu and Tong Guan and failed to detect Guo Yaoshi's defection in time; he was dismissed as academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and made intendant of Chongfu Palace on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 又責授朝議大夫、秘書少監、分司南京，隨州居住；

translations.literal: He was again demoted to court discussion grandee, vice director of the Secretariat, and commissioner in Nanjing, residing at Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again demoted to court discussion grandee and vice director of the Secretariat with duties in Nanjing, and ordered to reside at Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 又貶單州團練副使，象州安置。

translations.literal: He was further demoted to vice military commissioner of Danzhou and settled at Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was further demoted to vice military commissioner of Danzhou and exiled to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，內徙道州，尋放自便。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne he was moved inland to Daozhou, then released to go where he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne he was moved inland to Daozhou, then released to go where he pleased.

sentences.zh: 紹興初，復左中大夫。

translations.literal: Early in the Shaoxing era he was restored to left grandee of court.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shaoxing era he was restored to left grandee of court.

sentences.zh: 子辟章知泉州，迎安中往，未幾卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: His son Bichang governed Quanzhou and welcomed Anzhong there; he died not long after, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bichang governed Quanzhou and welcomed Anzhong there; he died not long afterward, at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 安中為文豐潤敏拔，尤工四六之制。

translations.literal: Anzhong's writing was rich, fluent, quick, and elevated; he was especially skilled in parallel prose.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhong wrote in a rich, fluent, quick, and elevated style and was especially skilled in parallel prose.

sentences.zh: 徽宗嘗宴睿謨殿，命安中賦詩百韻以紀其事。

translations.literal: Huizong once feasted at the Hall of Sagacious Deliberation and ordered Anzhong to compose a poem of a hundred rhymes to record the event.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong once feasted at the Hall of Sagacious Deliberation and ordered Anzhong to compose a hundred-rhyme poem to record the occasion.

sentences.zh: 詩成，嘗歎不已，令大書於殿屏，凡侍臣皆以副本賜之。

translations.literal: When the poem was finished the emperor sighed in admiration and had it written large on the hall screen; all attending ministers were given copies.
translations.idiomatic: When the poem was finished the emperor sighed in admiration and had it written in large characters on the hall screen; every attending minister was given a copy.

sentences.zh: 其見重如此。

translations.literal: He was esteemed to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 有《初寮集》七十六卷傳於世。

translations.literal: His Chuliao Collection in seventy-six juan has been transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Chuliao Collection in seventy-six juan has been handed down to later ages.

sentences.zh: 王襄 附

translations.literal: Wang Xiang, appended
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiang, appended

sentences.zh: 王襄，初名甯，鄧州南陽人，擢進士第。

translations.literal: Wang Xiang, originally named Ning, was a native of Nanyang in Dengzhou and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiang, originally named Ning, came from Nanyang in Dengzhou and passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 崇寧二年，以軍器監主簿言事稱旨，擢庫部員外郎，改光祿少卿，出察訪陝西。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongning, as registrar of the Directorate of Armaments he spoke on affairs to the emperor's satisfaction and was promoted to vice director of the Storehouse Bureau, then changed to vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and sent out to inspect Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chongning, as registrar of the Directorate of Armaments he spoke on policy to the emperor's satisfaction and was promoted to vice director of the Storehouse Bureau, then made vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and sent out to inspect Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 還，為顯謨閣待制、權知開封府。

translations.literal: On his return he was made awaiting academician of the Xianmo Hall and acting prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made awaiting academician of the Xianmo Hall and acting prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 府事浩穰，訟者株蔓千餘人，縲系滿獄。

translations.literal: Prefectural affairs were vast and tangled; litigants implicated more than a thousand people and the prisons were full of those in fetters.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural affairs were vast and tangled; litigants had implicated more than a thousand people and the prisons were packed with prisoners in fetters.

sentences.zh: 襄晝夜決遣，四旬俱盡；

translations.literal: Xiang judged cases day and night and cleared them all within forty days.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang judged cases day and night and cleared the entire backlog within forty days.

sentences.zh: 又閱月，獄再空。

translations.literal: After another month the prisons were empty again.
translations.idiomatic: After another month the prisons were empty again.

sentences.zh: 遷龍圖閣直學士、吏部侍郎，出知杭州；

translations.literal: He was transferred to direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and vice minister of Personnel, and sent out to govern Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and vice minister of Personnel, and sent out to govern Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 未至，改海州；

translations.literal: Before he arrived he was changed to Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could arrive he was reassigned to Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 又改應天府，徙鄆州。

translations.literal: He was again changed to Yingtianfu and transferred to Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again reassigned to Yingtianfu and then transferred to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 召為禮部尚書，移兵部，出知潁州，改永興軍。。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of Rites, moved to the Ministry of War, sent out to govern Yingzhou, and changed to Yongxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Minister of Rites, moved to the Ministry of War, sent out to govern Yingzhou, and then assigned to Yongxing Army.

sentences.zh: 蒲城妖賊王寧適同姓名，請更名宓。

translations.literal: The sorcerer-rebel Wang Ning of Pucheng happened to share his name; he requested to change his name to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: A sorcerer-rebel named Wang Ning in Pucheng happened to share his name; he requested to change his name to Mi.

sentences.zh: 為左司諫石公弼所劾，徙汝州，俄奪學士，提舉南京鴻慶宮。

translations.literal: Impeached by remonstrator of the Left Office Shi Gongbi, he was transferred to Ruzhou; soon his academician title was stripped and he was made intendant of Hongqing Palace in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Impeached by remonstrator of the Left Office Shi Gongbi, he was transferred to Ruzhou; soon his academician title was stripped and he was made intendant of Hongqing Palace in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 大觀三年，以集賢殿修撰知潭州，改兵部侍郎，使高麗。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daguan, as academician of the Hall for Collecting the Finest Writings he governed Tanzhou, was changed to vice minister of War, and sent as envoy to Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daguan, as academician of the Hall for Collecting the Finest Writings he governed Tanzhou, was made vice minister of War, and sent as envoy to Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 還對稱旨，詔賜名襄。

translations.literal: On returning from audience his responses pleased the emperor and an edict bestowed on him the name Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned and came before the throne his answers pleased the emperor, and an edict bestowed on him the name Xiang.

sentences.zh: 曆工部、吏部尚書，拜同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Minister of Works and Minister of Personnel and was appointed vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Minister of Works and Minister of Personnel and was appointed vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 坐薦引近侍，以延康殿學士罷知亳州；

translations.literal: For recommending a close attendant he was dismissed as academician of the Yankang Hall and made prefect of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: For recommending a close attendant he was dismissed as academician of the Yankang Hall and sent to govern Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 又坐交通郭天信落職，提舉嵩山崇福宮。

translations.literal: Again, for associating with Guo Tianxin he lost his post and was made intendant of Chongfu Palace on Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: Again, for associating with Guo Tianxin he lost his post and was made intendant of Chongfu Palace on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 久之，起知郢州，復學士秩，尋加資政殿學士，徙知淮寧府。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was recalled to govern Yingzhou, his academician rank was restored, and soon he was made academician of the Zizheng Hall and transferred to govern Huainingfu.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was recalled to govern Yingzhou, his academician rank was restored, and soon he was promoted to academician of the Zizheng Hall and transferred to Huainingfu.

sentences.zh: 以言事忤王黼，復提舉崇福宮。

translations.literal: For remonstrating on affairs and offending Wang Fu he was again made intendant of Chongfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: For speaking on policy in a way that offended Wang Fu he was again made intendant of Chongfu Palace.

sentences.zh: 宣和六年，起為河南尹。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xuanhe he was recalled as prefect of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xuanhe he was recalled as prefect of Henan.

sentences.zh: 金人再入，出為西道都總管，張杲副之。

translations.literal: When the Jin entered a second time he was sent out as commander-in-chief of the western route, with Zhang Gao as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin invaded again he was sent out as commander-in-chief of the western route, with Zhang Gao as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 高宗開大元帥府，襄以所部兵會于虞城縣。

translations.literal: When Gaozong opened the Grand Marshal's headquarters, Xiang joined him with his troops at Yucheng County.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong established the Grand Marshal's headquarters, Xiang brought his troops to join him at Yucheng County.

sentences.zh: 即位，命襄知河南府。

translations.literal: On the emperor's accession Xiang was ordered to govern Henan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, Xiang was appointed prefect of Henan.

sentences.zh: 襄初與趙野分總西北道諸軍，金人圍京師，徵兵入援，二人故迂道宿留。

translations.literal: Xiang had earlier divided command of the northwestern-route armies with Zhao Ye; when the Jin besieged the capital and troops were summoned for relief, the two deliberately took circuitous routes and delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang had earlier shared command of the northwestern-route armies with Zhao Ye; when the Jin besieged the capital and relief troops were summoned, the two deliberately took roundabout routes and lingered on the way.

sentences.zh: 至是，降寧遠軍節度副使，永州安置，卒。

translations.literal: At this time he was demoted to vice military commissioner of Ningyuan Army and ordered to reside at Yongzhou, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was then demoted to vice military commissioner of the Ningyuan Army, ordered to reside at Yongzhou, and died there.

sentences.zh: 趙野 附

translations.literal: Zhao Ye, appended
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ye, appended

sentences.zh: 趙野，開封人。

translations.literal: Zhao Ye was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ye came from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 登政和二年進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Zhenghe.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Zhenghe.

sentences.zh: 曆監察御史、殿中侍御史，試起居舍人兼太子舍人，俄遷中書舍人、給事中、大司成，拜刑部尚書、翰林學士。

translations.literal: He served in succession as investigating censor and palace censor, tested as attendant of the Secretariat and concurrent tutor of the crown prince, soon promoted to drafting attendant of the Secretariat, supervising censor, and grand director of studies, and appointed Minister of Justice and Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of investigating censor and palace censor, tested as attendant of the Secretariat and concurrent tutor of the crown prince, was soon promoted to drafting attendant, supervising censor, and grand director of studies, and was appointed Minister of Justice and Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 時蔡京、王黼更秉政，植黨相擠，一進一退，莫有能兩全者，野處之皆得其心，京、黼亦待之不疑。

translations.literal: At that time Cai Jing and Wang Fu alternated in holding power, planting factions to squeeze one another; as one advanced the other retreated, and none could satisfy both; Ye navigated this and won the hearts of both, and Jing and Fu also treated him without suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Cai Jing and Wang Fu alternated in power, each planting factions to squeeze the other; as one rose the other fell, and few could please both sides—yet Ye managed to win the trust of each, and neither Jing nor Fu suspected him.

sentences.zh: 宣和七年，拜尚書右丞，升左丞。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xuanhe he was appointed right vice director of the Department of State Affairs and promoted to left vice director.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xuanhe he was appointed right vice director of the Department of State Affairs and promoted to left vice director.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，為門下侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingkang he was vice director of the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingkang crisis he was vice director of the Gate.

sentences.zh: 徽宗東幸，詔野為行宮奉迎使。

translations.literal: When Huizong traveled east, an edict appointed Ye commissioner for welcoming the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong traveled east, an edict appointed Ye commissioner for welcoming the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 以左司諫陳公輔言，罷野行，出為北道都總管，顏岐副之。

translations.literal: On the remonstrance of remonstrator of the Left Office Chen Gongfu, Ye's mission was canceled; he was sent out as commander-in-chief of the northern route, with Yan Qi as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: On the remonstrance of remonstrator of the Left Office Chen Gongfu, Ye's mission was canceled; he was sent out as commander-in-chief of the northern route, with Yan Qi as deputy.

sentences.zh: 已而落職，提舉嵩山崇福宮。

translations.literal: Soon he was stripped of office and made intendant of Chongfu Palace on Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was stripped of office and made intendant of Chongfu Palace on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 元帥府建，命與范訥為宣撫司，守東京，尋帥師屯宛亭，以待王師。

translations.literal: When the Grand Marshal's headquarters was established he was ordered with Fan Ne to form a pacification commission and hold the Eastern Capital, then soon led troops to camp at Wanting to await the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Marshal's headquarters was established he was ordered with Fan Ne to form a pacification commission and hold the Eastern Capital, then soon led troops to camp at Wanting to await the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 王襄既責，野亦降安遠軍節度副使，邵州安置。

translations.literal: Once Wang Xiang was punished, Ye was also demoted to vice military commissioner of Anyuan Army and ordered to reside at Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Xiang was punished, Ye was likewise demoted to vice military commissioner of the Anyuan Army and ordered to reside at Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 建炎元年，復起知密州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyan he was again recalled to govern Mizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianyan he was again recalled to govern Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 時盜賊充斥山東，車駕如淮南，命令阻絕，野棄城去。

translations.literal: At that time bandits filled Shandong; as the imperial carriage moved toward the Huai region, orders were cut off and Ye abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: At that time bandits filled Shandong; as the imperial carriage moved toward the Huai region, orders ceased to arrive and Ye abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 軍校杜彥等乘間作亂，追野以歸。

translations.literal: The garrison officer Du Yan and others seized the moment to rebel and pursued Ye to bring him back.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison officer Du Yan and others seized the moment to rebel and pursued Ye to bring him back.

sentences.zh: 彥坐堂上數之曰：「汝知州而攜家先遁，此州之人，誰其為主？」

translations.literal: Yan sat in the hall and rebuked him, saying, "You were the prefect yet fled with your family first—who in this prefecture will take you as their lord?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan sat in the hall and rebuked him, saying, "You were the prefect yet fled with your family ahead of everyone—who in this prefecture would still call you their lord?"

sentences.zh: 野不能應，遂見殺。

translations.literal: Ye could not answer and was thereupon killed.
translations.idiomatic: Ye could not answer and was killed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 家屬悉為賊所分，唯子學老得免。

translations.literal: His household were all divided among the bandits; only his son Xuelao escaped.
translations.idiomatic: His household were all divided among the bandits; only his son Xuelao escaped.

sentences.zh: 曹輔 附

translations.literal: Cao Fu, appended
translations.idiomatic: Cao Fu, appended

sentences.zh: 曹輔，字載德，南劍州人。

translations.literal: Cao Fu, style name Zaide, was a native of Nanjianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Fu, whose style name was Zaide, came from Nanjianzhou.

sentences.zh: 第進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 政和二年，以通仕郎中詞學兼茂科，曆秘書省正字。
