translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenghe, through the dual examination in erudite letters and flourishing literary talent he served as rectifier in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenghe, through the dual examination in erudite letters and flourishing literary talent, he served as rectifier in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 自政和後，帝多微行，乘小轎子，數內臣導從。

translations.literal: After Zhenghe the emperor often traveled incognito, riding in a small palanquin with several eunuchs guiding him.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhenghe era the emperor often traveled incognito, riding in a small palanquin with a few eunuchs as guides.

sentences.zh: 置行幸局，局中以帝出日謂之有排當，次日未還，則傳旨稱瘡痍，不坐朝。

translations.literal: A Bureau for Imperial Excursions was established; within the bureau the day the emperor went out was called having a schedule, and if he did not return the next day an edict would be transmitted saying he was afflicted with sores and would not hold court.
translations.idiomatic: A Bureau for Imperial Excursions was established; the day the emperor went out was called having a schedule, and if he failed to return the next day an edict would announce that he was afflicted with sores and would not hold court.

sentences.zh: 始，民間猶未知。

translations.literal: At first the common people still did not know.
translations.idiomatic: At first the common people still did not know.

sentences.zh: 及蔡京謝表有「輕車小輦，七賜臨幸」，自是邸報聞四方，而臣僚阿順，莫敢言。

translations.literal: When Cai Jing's letter of thanks contained the phrase "light carriage and small palanquin, seven bestowals of imperial visits," thereafter the court gazette spread the news to the four quarters, while the officials fawned and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing's letter of thanks contained the phrase "light carriage and small palanquin, seven bestowals of imperial visits," the court gazette spread the news across the realm, while officials fawned and none dared speak.

sentences.zh: 輔上疏略曰：

translations.literal: Fu submitted a memorial in summary saying:
translations.idiomatic: Fu submitted a memorial that read in summary:

sentences.zh: 陛下厭居法宮，時乘小輿，出入廛陌之中、郊坰之外，極遊樂而後反。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is weary of dwelling in the regulated palace and from time to time rides a small carriage, going out among the market lanes and beyond the suburban fields, pursuing extreme pleasure before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is weary of dwelling in the regulated palace and from time to time rides a small carriage out among the market lanes and beyond the suburban fields, pursuing pleasure to the utmost before returning.

sentences.zh: 道塗之言始猶有忌，今乃談以為帝某日由某路適某所，某時而歸；

translations.literal: Talk along the roads at first was still cautious, but now people discuss which day the emperor went by which route to which place and at what hour he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Talk along the roads was at first still cautious, but now people discuss which day the emperor went by which route to which place and at what hour he returned.

sentences.zh: 又雲輿飾可辨而辟。

translations.literal: They also say the carriage ornaments can be recognized from afar.
translations.idiomatic: They also say the carriage ornaments can be recognized from afar.

sentences.zh: 臣不意陛下當宗廟社稷付託之重，玩安忽危，一至於此。

translations.literal: I did not expect that Your Majesty, bearing the heavy charge of the ancestral temples and altars of state, would treat security with neglect and danger with play, to reach this point.
translations.idiomatic: I did not expect that Your Majesty, bearing the heavy charge of the ancestral temples and altars of state, would treat security with neglect and danger with play, until matters reached this point.

sentences.zh: 夫君之與民，本以人合，合則為腹心，離則為楚、越，畔服之際在於斯須，甚可畏也。

translations.literal: Between ruler and people the bond is fundamentally made through human feeling; when united they are as heart and belly, when divided they are as Chu and Yue—the moment of turning away or submitting lies within an instant, and this is greatly to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Between ruler and people the bond is made through human feeling; when united they are heart and belly, when divided they are Chu and Yue—the moment of turning away lies within an instant, and this is greatly to be feared.

sentences.zh: 昔者仁祖視民如子。

translations.literal: In former times Emperor Ren treated the people as his children.
translations.idiomatic: In former times Emperor Ren treated the people as his children.

sentences.zh: 憫然惟恐其或傷。

translations.literal: He was full of pity and feared lest they be harmed in any way.
translations.idiomatic: He was full of pity and feared lest they suffer any harm.

sentences.zh: 一旦宮闈不禁，衛士輒逾禁城，幾觸寶瑟。

translations.literal: Once the inner palace was not secure and guards overstepped the forbidden city, nearly touching the imperial zither.
translations.idiomatic: Once the inner palace was breached and guards overstepped the forbidden city, nearly striking the imperial zither.

sentences.zh: 荷天之休，帝躬保祐。

translations.literal: Thanks to Heaven's blessing the emperor's person was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Heaven's blessing the emperor's person was preserved.

sentences.zh: 俚語有之，'盜憎主人'，主人何負于盜哉？

translations.literal: A common saying runs, "A thief hates his master"—what has the master done to the thief?
translations.idiomatic: A common saying runs, "A thief hates his master"—what has the master done to deserve the thief's hatred?

sentences.zh: 況今革冗員，斥濫奉，去浮屠，誅胥吏，蚩愚之民，豈能一一引咎安分？

translations.literal: Moreover, now redundant posts are cut, excessive stipends removed, Buddhist establishments reduced, and corrupt clerks punished—how can the foolish masses one by one accept blame and keep to their places?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, now redundant posts are cut, excessive stipends removed, Buddhist establishments reduced, and corrupt clerks punished—how can the foolish masses one by one accept blame and keep their places?

sentences.zh: 萬一當乘輿不戒之初，一夫不逞，包藏禍心，發蜂蠆之毒，奮獸窮之計，雖神靈垂護，然亦損威傷重矣。

translations.literal: If, when Your Majesty is incautious on an outing, a single man loses restraint, harbors a treacherous heart, and unleashes the poison of a hornet or the desperation of a cornered beast, even if spirits protect you, your majesty will still suffer loss of authority and grave injury.
translations.idiomatic: If, when Your Majesty is incautious on an outing, a single man loses restraint, harbors treachery, and unleashes the poison of a hornet or the desperation of a cornered beast, even if spirits protect you, your majesty will still suffer loss of authority and grave injury.

sentences.zh: 又況有臣子不忍言者，可不戒哉！

translations.literal: Moreover, there are matters that ministers cannot bear to speak of—should this not be guarded against!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, there are matters ministers cannot bear to speak of—should this not be guarded against!

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下深居高拱，淵默雷聲，臨之以穹昊至高之勢，行之以日月有常之度。

translations.literal: I pray that Your Majesty dwell deep and hold the throne high, silent as thunder, facing the realm with the supreme power of Heaven, and acting with the regular motion of sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: I pray that Your Majesty dwell deep and hold the throne high, silent as thunder, facing the realm with Heaven's supreme power, and acting with the regular motion of sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 及其出也，太史擇日，有司除道，三衛百官，以前以後。

translations.literal: When you go out, the grand astrologer chooses the day, the relevant offices clear the road, and the three guards and all officials precede and follow.
translations.idiomatic: When you go out, the grand astrologer chooses the day, the relevant offices clear the road, and the three guards and all officials precede and follow.

sentences.zh: 若曰省煩約費，以便公私，則臨時降旨，存所不可闕，損所未嘗用。

translations.literal: If the aim is to reduce trouble and expense for public and private benefit, then issue a temporary edict, retaining what cannot be omitted and cutting what has never been used.
translations.idiomatic: If the aim is to reduce trouble and expense for public and private benefit, then issue a temporary edict, retaining what cannot be omitted and cutting what has never been used.

sentences.zh: 雖非祖宗奮制，比諸微服晦跡，下同臣庶，堂陛陵夷，民生奸望，不猶愈乎？

translations.literal: Though this is not the strenuous restraint of the ancestors, compared with traveling in disguise and hiding your tracks, lowering yourself to the level of common subjects, degrading the hall and steps, and stirring wicked hopes among the people—is it not still better?
translations.idiomatic: Though this falls short of the ancestors' strenuous restraint, compared with traveling in disguise, hiding your tracks, lowering yourself to the level of common subjects, degrading the hall and steps, and stirring wicked hopes among the people—is it not still better?

sentences.zh: 上得疏，出示宰臣，令赴都堂審問。

translations.literal: The emperor received the memorial and showed it to the chief councilors, ordering Fu to go to the chief councilors' hall for examination.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received the memorial, showed it to the chief councilors, and ordered Fu to the chief councilors' hall for examination.

sentences.zh: 太宰餘深曰：「輔小官，何敢論大事？」

translations.literal: Grand Councilor Yu Shen said, "Fu is a petty official—how dare he discuss great affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Yu Shen said, "Fu is a petty official—how dare he discuss great affairs?"

sentences.zh: 輔對曰：「大官不言，故小官言之。

translations.literal: Fu replied, "Because great officials do not speak, a petty official speaks.
translations.idiomatic: Fu replied, "Because great officials do not speak, a petty official must speak.

sentences.zh: 官有大小，愛君之心，則一也。」

translations.literal: Officials may differ in rank, but the heart that loves the ruler is one."
translations.idiomatic: Officials may differ in rank, but the heart that loves the ruler is one."

sentences.zh: 少宰王黼陽顧左丞張邦昌、右丞李邦彥曰：「有是事乎？」

translations.literal: Junior Councilor Wang Fu turned to left vice director Zhang Bangchang and right vice director Li Bangyan and said, "Is there such a thing?"
translations.idiomatic: Junior Councilor Wang Fu turned to left vice director Zhang Bangchang and right vice director Li Bangyan and said, "Is there such a thing?"

sentences.zh: 皆應以不知。

translations.literal: Both answered that they did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Both answered that they did not know.

sentences.zh: 輔曰：「茲事雖裏巷細民無不知，相公當國，獨不知邪？

translations.literal: Fu said, "Though this matter is unknown even to alleyway commoners, you govern the state—do you alone not know it?
translations.idiomatic: Fu said, "Though even alleyway commoners know this matter, you govern the state—do you alone not know it?

sentences.zh: 曾此不知，焉用彼相！」

translations.literal: If you did not know this, of what use is such a councilor!"
translations.idiomatic: If you did not know this, of what use is such a councilor!"

sentences.zh: 黼怒其侵已，令吏從輔受辭。

translations.literal: Fu was angry at the affront to himself and had clerks take Fu's statement.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was angry at being affronted and had clerks take Fu's written statement.

sentences.zh: 輔操筆曰：「區區之心，一無所求，愛君而已。」

translations.literal: Fu took up the brush and wrote, "This petty heart seeks nothing at all—only to love the ruler."
translations.idiomatic: Fu took up the brush and wrote, "This petty heart seeks nothing at all—only to love the ruler."

sentences.zh: 退，待罪於家。

translations.literal: He withdrew and waited at home to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew and waited at home to be punished.

sentences.zh: 黼奏不重責輔，無以息浮言，遂編管郴州。

translations.literal: Fu memorialized that if Fu were not heavily punished the floating talk would not cease, and Fu was therefore registered and banished to Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu memorialized that if Fu were not heavily punished the rumors would not cease, and Fu was therefore registered and banished to Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 輔將言，知必獲罪，召子紳來，付以家事，乃閉戶草疏。

translations.literal: Before speaking Fu knew he would certainly be punished; he summoned his son Shen and entrusted him with household affairs, then shut his door and drafted the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Before speaking Fu knew he would certainly be punished; he summoned his son Shen and entrusted him with household affairs, then shut his door and drafted the memorial.

sentences.zh: 夕有惡鳥鳴屋極，聲若紡輪，心知其不祥，弗恤也。

translations.literal: In the evening an evil bird cried on the roof ridge, its sound like a spinning wheel; he knew in his heart this was inauspicious but paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: In the evening an evil bird cried on the roof ridge, its sound like a spinning wheel; he knew in his heart this was inauspicious but paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 處郴六年，黼當國不得移，輔亦怡然不介意。

translations.literal: He remained at Chen six years; while Fu held power Fu could not be transferred, yet Fu remained at ease and unconcerned.
translations.idiomatic: He remained at Chen six years; while Wang Fu held power he could not be transferred, yet Cao Fu remained at ease and unconcerned.

sentences.zh: 耿南仲 附

translations.literal: Geng Nanzhong, appended
translations.idiomatic: Geng Nanzhong, appended

sentences.zh: 耿南仲，開封府人。

translations.literal: Geng Nanzhong was a native of Kaifeng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Nanzhong came from Kaifeng prefecture.

sentences.zh: 與余深同年登第，曆提舉兩浙常平，徙河北西路，改轉運判官、提點廣南東路及夔州路刑獄、荊湖江西兩路轉運副使，入為戶部員外郎、辟雍司業，坐事罷知衢州。

translations.literal: He passed the examination in the same year as Yu Shen and served in succession as intendant of the Zhejiang Ever-Normal Granaries, was transferred to Hebei West Circuit, changed to transport vice-commissioner, commissioner for criminal affairs in the eastern circuit of Guangnan and in Kuizhou circuit, transport vice-commissioner of the Jinghu, Jiangxi, and Huguang circuits, and entered office as vice director of the Ministry of Revenue and director of studies at the Directorate of Education; for an offense he was dismissed to govern Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examination in the same year as Yu Shen and served as intendant of the Zhejiang Ever-Normal Granaries, was transferred to Hebei West Circuit, became transport vice-commissioner and commissioner for criminal affairs in eastern Guangnan and Kuizhou circuits and transport vice-commissioner in the Jinghu, Jiangxi, and Huguang circuits, then entered the capital as vice director of the Ministry of Revenue and director of studies at the Directorate of Education; for an offense he was dismissed to govern Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 政和二年，以禮部員外郎為太子右庶子，改定王、嘉王侍讀，俄試太子詹事、徽猷閣直學士，改寶文閣直學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenghe, as vice director of the Ministry of Rites he became right tutor of the crown prince, was changed to tutor to the Princes of Ding and Jia, soon tested as grand tutor of the crown prince and direct academician of the Huixian Hall, then changed to direct academician of the Baowen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenghe, as vice director of the Ministry of Rites he became right tutor of the crown prince, was changed to tutor to the Princes of Ding and Jia, soon tested as grand tutor of the crown prince and direct academician of the Huixian Hall, then made direct academician of the Baowen Hall.

sentences.zh: 在東宮十年。

translations.literal: He was in the Eastern Palace ten years.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Eastern Palace for ten years.

sentences.zh: 欽宗辭內禪，得疾，出臥福甯殿，宰相百官班候，日暮不敢退。

translations.literal: When Qinzong declined the internal abdication he fell ill and lay out in the Hall of Blessings and Tranquility; the chief councilors and all officials stood in attendance and at dusk dared not withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: When Qinzong declined the internal abdication he fell ill and lay out in the Hall of Blessings and Tranquility; chief ministers and all officials stood in attendance and at dusk dared not withdraw.

sentences.zh: 李邦彥曰：「皇太子素親耿南仲，可召之入。」

translations.literal: Li Bangyan said, "The crown prince has always been close to Geng Nanzhong—he may be summoned in."
translations.idiomatic: Li Bangyan said, "The crown prince has always been close to Geng Nanzhong—he may be summoned in."

sentences.zh: 南仲與吳敏至殿中侍疾。

translations.literal: Nanzhong and Wu Min came to the hall to attend on his illness.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhong and Wu Min came to the hall to attend on his illness.

sentences.zh: 明日，帝即位，拜資政殿大學士、簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor took the throne and Nanzhong was appointed academician of the Zizheng Hall and signer of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor took the throne and Nanzhong was appointed academician of the Zizheng Hall and signer of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 未幾，免簽書。

translations.literal: Before long he was relieved of the signing duty.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was relieved of the signing duty.

sentences.zh: 帝以南仲東宮舊臣，禮重之，賜宅一區，升尚書左丞、門下侍郎。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Nanzhong was an old servant of the Eastern Palace, treated him with special honor, granted him a residence, and promoted him to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs and vice director of the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Because Nanzhong had long served the Eastern Palace, the emperor treated him with special honor, granted him a residence, and promoted him to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs and vice director of the Gate.

sentences.zh: 金人再舉鄉京師，請割三鎮以和，議者多主戰守，唯南仲與吳幵堅欲割地。

translations.literal: When the Jin raised troops again and besieged the capital, demanding the cession of three prefectures for peace, many in deliberation favored fighting and defense, but only Nanzhong and Wu Kai firmly wished to cede territory.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin raised troops again and besieged the capital, demanding the cession of three prefectures for peace, many in council favored fighting and defense, but only Nanzhong and Wu Kai firmly wished to cede territory.

sentences.zh: 康王使軍前，請南仲偕。

translations.literal: The Prince of Kang was sent to the army front and asked that Nanzhong accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Kang was sent to the army front and asked that Nanzhong accompany him.

sentences.zh: 帝以其老，命其子中書舍人延禧代行。

translations.literal: The emperor, because he was old, ordered his son, drafting attendant of the Secretariat Yanxi, to go in his place.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, considering him too old, ordered his son Yanxi, drafting attendant of the Secretariat, to go in his place.

sentences.zh: 金人次洛陽，不復言三鎮，直請畫河為界。

translations.literal: When the Jin reached Luoyang they no longer spoke of the three prefectures but directly asked to fix the border at the river.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin reached Luoyang they no longer spoke of the three prefectures but directly demanded that the border be fixed at the river.

sentences.zh: 於是議遣大臣往，南仲以老辭，聶昌以親辭。

translations.literal: The court then deliberated sending a senior minister; Nanzhong declined on grounds of age and Nie Chang on grounds of kinship.
translations.idiomatic: The court then deliberated sending a senior minister; Nanzhong declined on grounds of age and Nie Chang on grounds of kinship.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，即令南仲出河東、昌出河北，議割地。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and at once ordered Nanzhong out to Hedong and Chang out to Hebei to negotiate the cession of territory.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly angered and at once ordered Nanzhong out to Hedong and Chang out to Hebei to negotiate the cession of territory.

sentences.zh: 初，南仲自謂事帝東宮，首當柄用，而吳敏、李綱越次進，位居己上，不能平。

translations.literal: At first Nanzhong thought that because he had served the emperor in the Eastern Palace he should be the first to wield power, yet Wu Min and Li Gang had risen out of turn and stood above him, and he could not be reconciled.
translations.idiomatic: At first Nanzhong thought that because he had served the emperor in the Eastern Palace he should be the first to wield power, yet Wu Min and Li Gang had risen out of turn and stood above him, and he could not accept it.

sentences.zh: 因每事異議，擯斥不附己者。

translations.literal: Therefore on every matter he took a different view and drove out those who did not attach themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore on every matter he took the opposite view and drove out those who would not attach themselves to him.

sentences.zh: 綱等謂不可和，而南仲力沮之，惟主和議，故戰守之備皆罷。

translations.literal: Gang and others said peace was impossible, but Nanzhong strenuously obstructed them and upheld only the peace policy, so preparations for war and defense were all abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Gang and others said peace was impossible, but Nanzhong strenuously obstructed them and upheld only the peace policy, so all preparations for war and defense were abandoned.

sentences.zh: 康王在相州，南仲偕金使王汭往衛州。

translations.literal: The Prince of Kang was at Xiangzhou; Nanzhong accompanied the Jin envoy Wang Rui to Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Kang was at Xiangzhou; Nanzhong accompanied the Jin envoy Wang Rui to Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 鄉兵穀殺汭，汭脫去，南仲獨趣衛，衛人不納。

translations.literal: Local militia at Gu killed Rui; Rui escaped, and Nanzhong alone hurried to Wei, but the people of Wei would not admit him.
translations.idiomatic: Local militia at Gu killed Rui; Rui escaped, and Nanzhong alone hurried to Wei, but the people of Wei would not admit him.

sentences.zh: 走相州，以上旨喻康王，起河北兵入衛京師，因連署募兵榜揭之，人情始安。

translations.literal: He fled to Xiangzhou, explained the imperial intent to the Prince of Kang, raised Hebei troops to defend the capital, and jointly signed a recruitment proclamation and posted it; popular feeling then settled.
translations.idiomatic: He fled to Xiangzhou, explained the imperial intent to the Prince of Kang, raised Hebei troops to defend the capital, and jointly signed a recruitment proclamation and posted it; popular feeling then settled.

sentences.zh: 二帝北行，南仲與文武官吏勸進。

translations.literal: When the two emperors were taken north, Nanzhong joined civil and military officials in urging the Prince of Kang to take the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the two emperors were taken north, Nanzhong joined civil and military officials in urging the Prince of Kang to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 高宗既即位，薄南仲為人，因其請老，罷為觀文殿大學士、提舉杭州洞霄宮。

translations.literal: Once Gaozong had taken the throne he looked down on Nanzhong's character; because Nanzhong asked to retire on grounds of age, he was dismissed as academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and made intendant of Dongxiao Palace in Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Once Gaozong had taken the throne he despised Nanzhong's character; because Nanzhong asked to retire on grounds of age, he was dismissed as academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and made intendant of Dongxiao Palace in Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 延禧以龍圖閣直學士知宣州。

translations.literal: Yanxi was made direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxi was made direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 已而言者論其主和誤國罪，詔鐫學士秩，延禧亦落職與祠。

translations.literal: Soon critics charged the crime of pursuing peace and harming the state; an edict stripped his academician rank, and Yanxi also lost his post and was given a temple sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: Soon critics charged him with pursuing peace at the cost of the state; an edict stripped his academician rank, and Yanxi also lost his post and was given a temple sinecure.

sentences.zh: 尋責南仲臨江軍居住。

translations.literal: Soon Nanzhong was ordered to reside at Linjiang Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Nanzhong was ordered to reside at Linjiang Army.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞張澂又言：「南仲趣李綱往救河東，以致師潰，蓋不恤國事，用此報讎。」

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Zhang Cheng again said, "Nanzhong urged Li Gang to go rescue Hedong, causing the army to collapse—he plainly cared nothing for state affairs and used this to settle a grudge."
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Zhang Cheng again said, "Nanzhong urged Li Gang to go rescue Hedong, causing the army to collapse—he plainly cared nothing for state affairs and used this to settle a personal grudge."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「南仲誤淵聖，天下共知，朕嘗欲手劍擊之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Nanzhong wronged the Profound Sage—everyone knows it—and I once wished to strike him with my own sword."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Nanzhong wronged the Profound Sage—everyone knows it—and I once wished to strike him with my own sword."

sentences.zh: 命降授別駕，安置南雄，行至吉州卒。

translations.literal: He was ordered demoted to assistant prefect and settled at Nanxiong; on the road he reached Jizhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered demoted to assistant prefect and exiled to Nanxiong; on the road he reached Jizhou and died.

sentences.zh: 建炎四年，復觀文殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianyan he was again made academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianyan he was again made academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature.

sentences.zh: 王㝢 附

translations.literal: Wang Yu, appended
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu, appended

sentences.zh: 王㝢，字元忠，江州人。

translations.literal: Wang Yu, style name Yuanzhong, was a native of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu, whose style name was Yuanzhong, came from Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 父易簡，資政殿大學士兼侍講。

translations.literal: His father Yijian was academician of the Zizheng Hall and concurrent reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yijian was academician of the Zizheng Hall and concurrent reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 㝢曆校書郎、著作佐郎、度支員外郎兼充編修官、國子司業，為起居舍人，改中書舍人兼蕃衍宅直講。

translations.literal: Yu served in succession as proofreader, assistant editor, vice director of the Revenue Bureau and concurrent compiler, and vice director of studies of the Directorate of Education, became attendant of the Secretariat, and was changed to drafting attendant of the Secretariat and concurrent lecturer at the Fanxi Residence.
translations.idiomatic: Yu rose through the posts of proofreader, assistant editor, vice director of the Revenue Bureau and concurrent compiler, and vice director of studies of the Directorate of Education, became attendant of the Secretariat, and was made drafting attendant and concurrent lecturer at the Fanxi Residence.

sentences.zh: 欽宗立，以給事中命兼邇英殿經筵侍講，轉吏部侍郎，升禮部尚書、翰林學士。

translations.literal: When Qinzong took the throne he was ordered as supervising censor to serve concurrently as lecturer at the Eying Hall classics lecture, transferred to vice minister of Personnel, and promoted to Minister of Rites and Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Qinzong took the throne he was ordered as supervising censor to serve concurrently as lecturer at the Eying Hall classics lecture, transferred to vice minister of Personnel, and promoted to Minister of Rites and Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 康王之使金也，以㝢為尚書左丞副之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Kang was sent as envoy to the Jin, Yu was appointed left vice director of the Department of State Affairs as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Kang was sent as envoy to the Jin, Yu was appointed left vice director of the Department of State Affairs as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 㝢憚行，假夢兆丐免，易簡亦上書以請。

translations.literal: Yu feared the journey and, citing a dream omen, begged to be excused; Yijian also submitted a memorial requesting the same.
translations.idiomatic: Yu feared the journey and, citing a dream omen, begged to be excused; Yijian also submitted a memorial asking the same on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 上震怒，追毀左丞命，降單州團練副使，新州安置，並易簡宮祠黜之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, revoked the appointment as left vice director, demoted Yu to vice military commissioner of Danzhou and settled him at Xinzhou, and also stripped Yijian of his palace sinecure and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, revoked the appointment as left vice director, demoted Yu to vice military commissioner of Danzhou and exiled him to Xinzhou, and also stripped Yijian of his palace sinecure and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 建炎四年，賊馬進破江州，易簡等三百人俱被害。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianyan the bandit Ma Jin broke Jiangzhou; Yijian and three hundred others were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianyan the bandit Ma Jin captured Jiangzhou; Yijian and three hundred others were all killed.

sentences.zh: 論曰：三代之後，有天下而長久者，漢、唐、宋爾。

translations.literal: The commentary says: After the Three Dynasties, those who held the realm long were Han, Tang, and Song alone.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: After the Three Dynasties, only Han, Tang, and Song held the realm for long.

sentences.zh: 漢、唐末世，朋黨相確，小人在位，然猶有君子扶持遷延，浸微浸滅；

translations.literal: At the end of Han and Tang, factions clashed and petty men held office, yet there were still gentlemen who supported and prolonged the decline, which grew faint and then vanished.
translations.idiomatic: At the ends of Han and Tang, factions clashed and petty men held office, yet gentlemen still supported the state and prolonged its decline, which grew faint and then vanished.

sentences.zh: 未有純用小人，至於主辱國播，如宋中葉之烈也。

translations.literal: Never before had petty men been employed exclusively, to the point of the ruler's humiliation and the realm's dispersal, as fiercely as in the middle Song.
translations.idiomatic: Never before had petty men been employed exclusively, to the point of the ruler's humiliation and the realm's dispersal, as fiercely as in the middle Song.

sentences.zh: 蔡京以紹述為羅，張端官、修士而盡之，上箝下錮，其術巧矣。

translations.literal: Cai Jing used the doctrine of continuing the reforms as a net, promoted petty officials and cultivated scholars to fill it, and clamped those above while shackling those below—his method was cunning.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing used the doctrine of continuing the reforms as a net, promoted petty officials and cultivated scholars to fill it, and clamped those above while shackling those below—his method was cunning.

sentences.zh: 徽宗亦頗悟，間用鄭居中、王黼、李邦彥輩，褫京柄權。

translations.literal: Huizong also came to some understanding and from time to time employed Zheng Juzhong, Wang Fu, Li Bangyan, and their like to strip Jing of power.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong also came to some understanding and from time to time employed Zheng Juzhong, Wang Fu, Li Bangyan, and their like to strip Jing of power.

sentences.zh: 以不肖易不肖，猶去野葛而代烏喙也，庸愈哉！

translations.literal: To replace the unworthy with the unworthy is like removing wild kudzu and substituting monkshood—how is it any improvement!
translations.idiomatic: To replace the unworthy with the unworthy is like removing wild kudzu and substituting monkshood—how is that any improvement!

sentences.zh: 當是時，王、蔡二黨，階京者芘京，締黼者右黼，援麗省台，迭相指嗾，徼功挑患，汴、洛既震，則恇縮無策，苟生丐和。

translations.literal: At that time the Wang and Cai factions—those who rose through Jing sheltered Jing, those who bonded with Fu supported Fu—filled the provincial and metropolitan offices, directing one another in turn, seeking merit and provoking disaster; once Bian and Luoyang were shaken they shrank back without strategy and begged for peace to save their lives.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Wang and Cai factions—those who rose through Jing sheltered Jing, those who bonded with Fu supported Fu—filled the provincial and metropolitan offices, directing one another in turn, seeking merit and provoking disaster; once Bian and Luoyang were shaken they shrank back without strategy and begged for peace merely to save their lives.

sentences.zh: 彼邦彥、安中、深、敏輩誤國之罪，當正其僇，而欽、高二君徒從竄典，信失刑矣。

translations.literal: The crimes of Bangyan, Anzhong, Shen, Min, and their like in harming the state ought to have been punished with the proper penalty, yet the two rulers Qin and Gao merely followed banishment statutes—truly a failure of justice.
translations.idiomatic: The crimes of Bangyan, Anzhong, Shen, Min, and their like in harming the state ought to have received proper punishment, yet Emperors Qin and Gao merely followed banishment statutes—truly a failure of justice.

sentences.zh: 恪既預推戴，署狀乃死，無足贖者。

translations.literal: Ke had already taken part in installing Zhang Bangchang; after signing his name he died—there is nothing to redeem.
translations.idiomatic: Ke had already taken part in installing Zhang Bangchang; after signing his name he died—there is nothing to redeem.

sentences.zh: 輔以小臣劘上，面譙大臣，坐斥不變，獨終始無朋與，其賢矣乎。

translations.literal: Fu, a petty official, remonstrated with the emperor, rebuked the chief councilors to their faces, and sat in dismissal without change, alone from first to last without faction—was he not worthy?
translations.idiomatic: Fu, a petty official, remonstrated with the emperor, rebuked the chief councilors to their faces, and sat in dismissal without wavering, alone from first to last without faction—was he not worthy?
